sentences.text: Jaklapallisaurus was a type of unaysaurid sauropodomorph dinosaur.
Its species name, asymmetricus, refers to a highly asymmetrical astragalus bone seen from the distal end.
The holotype specimen, the specific fossil the species is based on, was collected from the Upper Maleri Formation in the Pranhita–Godavari Basin.
Fernando E. Novas, Martin D. Ezcurra, Sankar Chatterjee, and Tharavat S. Kutty first named Jaklapallisaurus in 2011.
Phylogenetic analysis places Jaklapallisaurus as the sister taxon to Macrocollum within the family Unaysauridae.
This animal lived in what is now central India during the Late Triassic period.
It existed between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago during the Norian to Rhaetian stages.
